title: Word Recognition
before:
The Word Recognition section, in the Active View of Reading, is probably the most aligned with Scarborough's Rope. It includes phonological awareness, alphabetic principles, phonics, decoding, and sight words.
Each accordion below has self-paced asynchronous professional learning modules with a mix of video and text resources, opportunities for application and reflection, and contact hours.
 If you would like a contact hour for your work, please e-mail Kathy.Bertini@maine.gov

notes: 1 section header — too few for a contents list.
611 words with no section headers at all — the biggest single improvement available here.

decisions.label: Set an over-long heading as the paragraph it is
decisions.why: 2 headings run past 100 characters — the longest here is 209. "The Word Recognition section, in the Active View of Read…" is body text that was set as a heading to make it stand out, so it is announced as a section of the page and, at h2, written into the contents list as a link. It becomes a paragraph. Any anchor on it is kept, so existing links still land, and not a word changes.

decisions.label: Rebuild the heading outline
decisions.why: 1 heading sits at a level the page never opens — "If you would like a contact hour for your work, " is an h6 with no h5 above it, so it is neither announced nor styled as the sub-section it is. Each heading moves to one level below whatever encloses it.

decisions.label: Turn the headings into section headers
decisions.why: 1 heading is plain text where every other page uses a section header, so the page reads as one continuous wall instead of parts.

decisions.label: Drop the dash once the link is set apart
decisions.why: 3 of those items separate the link from its description with a dash. The link is now set in the display face at a larger size with a chevron after it, so the dash marks a boundary that is already unmistakable. Only the separator is removed — no word changes.

decisions.label: Separate a link from its description
decisions.why: 8 list items open with a link and then explain it, all at the same weight — so the thing you can click is no easier to find than the sentence about it. The link becomes the item and the explanation sits under it.

decisions.label: Make a loose address look like an address
decisions.why: 1 email address sits in the body of this page rather than in a contact block, drawn exactly like every other link — so the one that opens a mail window looks the same as the ones that go to web pages. The chip carries the same envelope the banner's contact link uses. The address itself does not change.

decisions.label: Use this paragraph as the page description
decisions.why: It is the page’s own opening paragraph, moved into the banner rather than rewritten.
decisions.value: The Word Recognition section, in the Active View of Reading, is probably the most aligned with Scarborough's Rope. It includes phonological awareness, alphabetic principles, phonics, decoding, and sight words.

decisions.label: Start a description with a capital
decisions.why: 5 descriptions begin with a small letter, because they used to run on from the link after a dash. The dash is gone and the link now sits above in its own face, so each description opens a line of its own. One character changes and only ever the first.
